feature.title: Surgical Robotics Race Heats Up as J&J Installs First OTTAVA, Medtronic Hugo Clears General Surgery — While Tubeless Insulin Pumps and AI Diagnostics Post Hard Clinical Numbers
feature.summary: November 2026 is shaping up as a landmark month for medtech deployment, with two competing surgical robots achieving major U.S. milestones simultaneously: J&J's OTTAVA became the first table-integrated soft-tissue robot commercially installed in a U.S. hospital, while Medtronic's Hugo gained expanded FDA clearance covering roughly 3.5 million annual general surgery procedures. On the diabetes front, both Tandem and MiniMed received clearances for 7-day tubeless insulin delivery systems within days of each other, igniting a new competitive chapter. Meanwhile, real-world clinical evidence continued to mature, with the MASAI mammography RCT confirming a 44% radiologist workload reduction, a McGill AI triage model hitting AUC 0.86 across 526,000 ED visits, and Insilico Medicine's AI-discovered drug rentosertib advancing into Phase III after demonstrating a +98.4 mL lung-capacity gain versus placebo in IPF patients.

highlights.label: Biggest story
highlights.text: J&J's OTTAVA became the first commercially installed table-integrated surgical robot in the U.S. at Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center on November 19, 2026, the same week Medtronic's Hugo won expanded FDA clearance for six general surgery procedure categories.

highlights.label: Key trend
highlights.text: The tubeless automated insulin delivery market transformed overnight as both Tandem Mobi and MiniMed Fit received FDA clearances for 7-day wear within days of each other, tripling the number of tubeless AID options in the U.S.

highlights.label: To watch
highlights.text: Insilico Medicine's AI-discovered drug rentosertib has entered Phase III for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis after Phase IIa data showed a clinically meaningful +98.4 mL FVC gain—if Phase III replicates these results, it would be the first FDA-approved fully AI-designed drug.

articles.title: J&J Announces First Commercial Installation of the OTTAVA Robotic Surgical System at Memorial Hermann Health System
articles.snippet: Johnson & Johnson MedTech announced on November 19, 2026, that Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center in Houston became the first U.S. hospital to install the OTTAVA robotic surgical system under its early access commercial program. The FDA-designated system — the world's first authorized table-integrated soft-tissue robotic platform — was cleared in July 2026 for ten upper abdominal general surgery procedures, and Memorial Hermann had previously served as a clinical trial site for the FORTE IDE study supporting that authorization.
articles.result: First U.S. commercial OTTAVA installation; FDA-cleared for 10 procedures

articles.title: Medtronic's Hugo Robot Gets Expanded FDA Clearance in General Surgery
articles.snippet: On November 17, 2026, the FDA cleared Medtronic's Hugo RAS system for general surgery via expanded 510(k), covering gallbladder removals, small bowel resections, gastric bypass, hernia repairs, and appendectomies — procedures Medtronic estimates account for approximately 3.5 million annual U.S. surgeries. The clearance arrives less than one year after Hugo's initial December 2025 FDA clearance in urology, and general surgery is already Hugo's fastest-growing procedure mix outside the United States.
articles.result: Cleared for 6 general surgery categories covering ~3.5M U.S. annual cases

articles.title: MiniMed Fit FDA Clearance: World's First Tubeless Insulin Pump with Up to Seven-Day Wear and Zero Interruptions
articles.snippet: The FDA cleared MiniMed Fit on November 16, 2026, marking MiniMed's first tubeless insulin pump and the third tubeless AID system cleared in the U.S. The device offers up to seven days of wear without recharging or cartridge changes, a 300-unit insulin capacity — 50% more than rivals — and SmartGuard automated insulin delivery technology, which in real-world studies has achieved up to 80% time-in-range overall and 91% overnight time-in-range.
articles.result: 80% time-in-range in real-world SmartGuard studies; 7-day wear cleared

articles.title: Tandem Wins FDA Clearance for Tubeless Automated Insulin Delivery System with 7-Day Wear
articles.snippet: Tandem Diabetes Care received FDA 510(k) clearance on November 12, 2026, for a tubeless cartridge and infusion set converting the existing Mobi pump into a wearable device cleared for up to seven days — the longest infusion-set wear of any tubeless AID system. In the CIRCUIT clinical trial, pregnant patients using Tandem's Control-IQ+ algorithm spent 65.4% of time in the pregnancy-specific glucose range versus 50.3% with standard care (p < 0.001), and in the 2IQP trial the algorithm lowered HbA1c by 0.9 percentage points versus 0.3 with CGM alone in type 2 diabetes.
articles.result: 65.4% vs 50.3% pregnancy-range time in CIRCUIT trial (p<0.001)

articles.title: McGill AI Model Predicts Hospital Admission at Triage with AUC 0.86 Across 526,000 ED Visits
articles.snippet: A retrospective cohort study published November 10, 2026 in JMIR Medical Informatics evaluated a gradient-boosting machine learning model on 526,145 adult emergency department visits across two McGill University Health Centre hospitals, finding it could predict hospital admission at triage with an AUC of 0.86, outperforming a logistic regression baseline of 0.84. Subgroup analyses confirmed consistent performance across age, sex, and both hospital sites, with SHAP explainability identifying age, triage acuity scale, arrival mode, vital signs, and prior hospitalizations as the strongest predictors.
articles.result: AUC 0.86 for ED admission prediction at triage across 526,145 visits

articles.title: AI-Supported Mammography (MASAI Trial): 44% Radiologist Workload Reduction, 29% More Cancers Detected, 12% Fewer Interval Cancers
articles.snippet: Two-year follow-up results of the MASAI randomized controlled trial — the first completed RCT of AI-supported mammography screening — showed a 44% reduction in screen-reading workload for radiologists, 29% more cancers detected without increasing false positives, and 81% of cancer cases detected at screening in the AI arm versus 74% in standard double-reading. At two-year follow-up, 12% fewer interval cancers were detected in the AI arm, with AI catching smaller and less aggressive tumors including a 27% reduction in non-luminal A subtypes.
articles.result: 44% workload cut, 29% more cancers detected, 12% fewer interval cancers

articles.title: Insilico Medicine's AI-Discovered Drug Rentosertib Enters Phase III After +98.4 mL Lung Capacity Gain in Phase IIa RCT
articles.snippet: Insilico Medicine's rentosertib — a TNIK inhibitor fully designed by generative AI — showed a mean forced vital capacity improvement of +98.4 mL at 12 weeks in its 71-patient Phase IIa trial versus a -20.3 mL decline in the placebo group, the first time a fully AI-designed drug achieved positive proof-of-concept data in a randomized human trial. Building on these Phase IIa results published in Nature Medicine, Insilico initiated a 320-patient Phase III trial (GENESIS-IPF-3) in July 2026, dosed its first Phase III patient in September, and received FDA Fast Track designation for a second AI-discovered candidate (ISM6331) in advanced mesothelioma.
articles.result: +98.4 mL FVC gain vs -20.3 mL placebo decline at 12 weeks (Phase IIa)

articles.title: Masimo Receives FDA Clearance for smartSedLine Brain Function Monitor — Seventh Clearance in 2026
articles.snippet: Masimo, a Danaher company, received FDA 510(k) clearance on November 18, 2026, for its smartSedLine next-generation brain function monitoring system, which features an enhanced Patient State Index algorithm engineered to deliver faster induction responses and maintain stability during faint EEG signals. The clearance marks Masimo's seventh FDA authorization in 2026 and intensifies competition with Medtronic's historically dominant Bispectral Index technology in the depth-of-anesthesia monitoring market.
articles.result: 7th FDA clearance in 2026; faster PSi response confirmed under low EEG power

articles.title: Sine Health Receives FDA Clearance for First Smartphone-Only Essential Tremor Monitoring Device
articles.snippet: Sine Health (formerly Nordic Kinetics) received FDA 510(k) clearance (K261026) on November 15, 2026, for Sine — the first FDA-cleared device to monitor essential tremor using only a smartphone's existing sensors, requiring no additional hardware. The passive background monitoring system gives clinicians a continuous, objective view of how a patient's tremor changes between visits, addressing a critical gap for the estimated 7 million Americans with essential tremor who are frequently under-optimized on medication due to reliance on brief, intermittent clinical observations.
articles.result: First FDA-cleared smartphone-only tremor monitor; 7M Americans addressable

articles.title: FDA Clears AI Digital Cervical Cytology Slide Imaging System and Prognostic MCI Software as Class II Devices
articles.source: Alston & Bird Health Care Week in Review
articles.snippet: On November 4, 2026, the FDA issued two separate final orders classifying AI-driven diagnostic tools as Class II (special controls) devices: a digital cervical cytology slide imaging system with an AI algorithm for cervical cancer screening, and prognostic assessment software for mild cognitive impairment. Both classifications establish the regulatory framework for clinical deployment, signaling the FDA's continued commitment to integrating AI into high-stakes diagnostic pathways while ensuring performance benchmarks through special controls.
articles.result: Two AI diagnostic tools officially classified Class II; cleared for clinical use

articles.title: Only 3 of 1,357 FDA-Cleared AI Medical Devices Tested on Patient Outcomes, PLOS Digital Health Analysis Finds
articles.snippet: A systematic audit published August 19, 2026 in PLOS Digital Health by University of Toronto researchers found that of 1,357 AI-based medical devices FDA-authorized for patient care, only 34 were linked to registered clinical trials, only 12 had peer-reviewed manuscripts, and only 3 had been evaluated on patient-centered outcomes such as mortality, stroke, hospitalization, or quality of life. The findings — described by the authors as far thinner than expected — have galvanized calls for outcome-based evidence requirements before FDA clearance of AI medical devices.
articles.result: Only 3/1,357 FDA-cleared AI devices tested on patient survival or QoL
